objective:
Autonomously develop the TabDat Rust port by executing the roadmap in bounded agentic loops — one loop = one target slice = one PR = one meaningful development unit — continuing until blocked or the user stops, with GitHub issues kept current so the user is notified of problems and CI fixed before moving on.

Success criteria:
- Each merged PR corresponds to exactly one roadmap slice with recorded contract and acceptance evidence; roadmap checkboxes are updated only with evidence (source, tests, CI links, ADRs).
- `main` stays green: local checks (fmt, check, test, clippy) and hosted CI pass on the latest revision before every merge; CI failures are fixed before the next slice starts.
- Problems found locally (bugs, CI failures, blockers, contract gaps) are proactively created/updated as GitHub issues with clear titles so the user is easily notified.
- A report is delivered to the user at each phase exit gate and whenever the loop stops.

Boundaries:
- In scope: remaining roadmap slices (Phase 1 completion → Phase 15), CI fixes, ADRs, migration decision log, docs/spec alignment, GH issue maintenance.
- Out of scope: changes to the Python repository, features or refactors not in the roadmap, force-push, bypassing branch protections, marking phases complete by inference.

Constraints:
- Follow AGENTS.md: TDD for behavior changes, functional-first design, safe Rust by default, ADRs for major backend/FFI/packaging decisions, no silent tolerance widening, 2-space indentation.
- Commits, pushes, PR creation, and merges into `main` are authorized for this autonomous roadmap request only; a newer user restriction takes precedence.
- One integration owner; serialize overlapping writes; delegate bounded work to safe-agent children when useful.
- Statistical parity requires trusted references plus the Python oracle; recover pinned oracle evidence before claiming parity.

Verification contract:
- Per slice: focused tests added first; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` pass locally; hosted CI green on the merged revision; roadmap + docs updated with evidence links; PR diff reviewed and blocking findings resolved before merge.
- At each phase exit gate: verify every gate item against evidence and report to the user.

If blocked: stop the loop, record the blocker (with evidence and needed input) in a GitHub issue, and ask the user.
